mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the expected S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to tightened financing conditions and reduced corporate investment demand.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the prior month's return (t-test p > 0.05), or the FEDFUNDS change is not above 0.25% in any month during the window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) below the prior month's level, accompanied by a decline in consumer payrolls (PAYEMS), predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market weakness dampens consumer confidence and corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous_month PAYEMS AND PAYEMS < previous_quarter PAYEMS
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the 60-day forward returns are not consistently negative when the trigger occurs (average p-value > 0.10 across all such windows).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) grows faster than consumer demand proxies (HOUST), the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to supply-side expansion supporting future earnings.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth rate > HOUST growth rate over the prior month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows where the trigger occurs, the forward return is not statistically positive (Rank IC < 0.05) or the supply-demand gap reverses direction within 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive month of declining consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% suggests disinflation, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as market participants anticipate rate cuts later in the quarter.
failure_condition: Over 20 such windows, the 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) or the CPIAUCSL re-enters inflationary territory within 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% triggers a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as the labor market tightening is interpreted as a sign of economic strength and potential rate stability.
failure_condition: In 50 such triggered windows, the forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the UNRATE recovers within 60 days without a subsequent positive return.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly retail sales (not in observable list; fallback: use HOUST as proxy for consumption) fall for two consecutive months while manufacturing employment (not in observable list; fallback: use INDPRO) remains flat, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to weak consumption momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < previous_month HOUST AND HOUST <= previous_quarter HOUST AND INDPRO == previous_month INDPRO
failure_condition: Across 10 such windows, the 60-day forward returns are not consistently negative (average p-value > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer activity (HOUST) above their 12-month averages predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals broad-based demand recovery.
failure_condition: In 30 such triggered windows, the forward return is not statistically positive (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in residential construction (not directly observable; fallback: use INDPRO as proxy for building activity) over three months predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return due to weakening capital spending and reduced future earnings visibility.
failure_condition: Over 12 such windows, the 60-day forward returns are not consistently negative (average p-value > 0.10).
